one_line: Play The Secret of Monkey Island through ChatGPT using structured WebMCP game controls.
what_it_does: Runs the DOS game in browser WebAssembly and exposes semantic observation and action tools for an agent to play, inspect, navigate, choose dialogue, and save progress.
leverage_rationale: Structured semantic game state and actions are substantially more reliable than a general agent interpreting pixels and clicking a canvas, though the game itself remains playable manually.
leverage_evidence: About text describes a SCUMM semantic bridge and seven WebMCP tools.
Tools cover room observation, inventory, destinations, verbs, dialogue, waiting, and save/new-game operations.
Frame sheet visibly shows intentional Monkey Island product presentation, but not an end-to-end agent gameplay run.
execution_rationale: The implementation description is unusually concrete and the live demo is reported alive, but the submitted visual evidence is primarily a talking-head presentation and does not demonstrate the central gameplay workflow end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Description specifies ScummVM compiled to WebAssembly, pinned source patches, C++ bridge, TypeScript controller, and WebMCP adapter.
Demo is listed alive.
Frame evidence shows the presenter holding The Secret of Monkey Island cover; it does not show the application or gameplay.
impact_rationale: It offers a credible and appealing way to explore a classic adventure game with conversational assistance and agent play, especially for experimentation with legacy software interfaces.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets playing, asking for help, and letting an agent attempt the game.
Browser-local game files and semantic state address practical privacy and interaction concerns.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP to expose a 35-year-old SCUMM game running in WebAssembly is a memorable, technically ambitious interaction model beyond a conventional website.
creativity_evidence: About text frames the project as testing whether WebMCP can describe a legacy game inside WebAssembly.
Semantic game-engine bridge is a novel synthesis of classic adventure gameplay and agent control.
usability_note: Conversational play and browser-local files are promising, but setup and occasional screenshot fallback may add friction.
red_flags: Submitted frame sheets do not show the claimed product workflow.
standouts: Semantic WebMCP bridge into a legacy SCUMM engine.
advance_reason: Distinctive, technically ambitious agent-native game integration with a credible live demo, despite thin direct execution evidence.

one_line: An agent prepares code-review findings while humans approve or dismiss them inline.
what_it_does: Turns pull-request review into a shared queue where an agent reviews one or many PRs, surfaces findings in the normal diff, and keeps every finding private until reviewer judgment.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools let an agent review and organize PRs while preserving human ownership and precise inline findings; general UI driving is markedly less reliable for queue-wide review and line-level context.
leverage_evidence: About text lists review-one, review-queue, and decision-needed tools.
Findings are presented below relevant changed lines and remain private drafts until approval.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows a code diff, Civium draft finding, and Approve/Dismiss controls.
execution_rationale: The packaging and described surfaces agree on a coherent human-in-the-loop review workflow, with only minor uncertainty because direct video evidence is unavailable.
execution_evidence: Demo is listed alive and eight gallery images are reported.
Screenshot shows a pull-request-like diff with an inline draft finding and reviewer actions.
Description covers queue, no-findings, inline context, draft state, and GitHub extension surfaces.
impact_rationale: Code review is a real, attention-intensive workflow, and surfacing candidate issues without auto-publishing directly addresses reviewer fatigue while retaining judgment.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies sustained attention across every changed line as the problem.
Human approval is required before findings are published.
No-finding PRs can be skipped, focusing attention on changes needing review.
creativity_rationale: Human-owned AI draft review is a thoughtful synthesis with a useful workflow distinction, though AI code review itself is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Private-draft-first interaction model separates preparation from publication.
Shared queue plus inline findings integrates agent assistance into the existing review flow.
usability_note: Inline context and explicit Approve/Dismiss actions are clear; GitHub extension setup may add friction.
standouts: Strong human-ownership boundary: nothing is published merely because the agent found it.
advance_reason: Strong practical workflow, coherent evidence, and meaningful WebMCP-enabled collaboration.

one_line: An agent-native mission workspace for researching evidence and designing auditable interventions.
what_it_does: Converts a natural-language real-world objective into structured discovery, comparison, evidence inspection, risk assessment, planning, and human approval steps.
leverage_rationale: The concept is explicitly built around shared human-agent state and structured mission tools; a general agent scraping and clicking across heterogeneous evidence would not replicate the proposed auditable workflow comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Pitch calls it agent-native infrastructure and lists structured WebMCP operations.
About text describes discover, inspect, compare, learn from failures, assess risk, and request approval as one workflow.
No frame sheets or gallery images were submitted, so live behavior is not directly shown.
execution_rationale: The written scope is ambitious but evidence is extremely thin: no frame sheets and zero gallery images, leaving the central workflow unverified.
execution_evidence: Demo is listed alive.
Packet contains no submitted video frame sheets and no gallery images.
About text provides extensive claimed functionality but not direct visual proof.
impact_rationale: The proposed audience—people managing difficult real-world infrastructure goals under constraints—has serious information and decision needs, and the auditable evidence-to-intervention workflow is a credible fit if realized.
impact_evidence: Example objective concerns improving water reliability with limited budget.
Workflow explicitly surfaces evidence, risks, prior failures, and unknowns before approval.
creativity_rationale: The human + agent + application + real-world systems interaction model is unusually ambitious and conceptually original for the challenge.
creativity_evidence: About text explicitly frames a new interaction model beyond an AI assistant.
Mission-based evidence and intervention planning are pursued as a structured auditable system.
usability_note: Natural-language mission framing could be accessible, but no visual workflow evidence supports usability claims.
red_flags: No frame sheets or gallery images; central product claims cannot be visually checked.
standouts: Ambitious shared-state model for real-world mission planning.
advance_reason: High concept potential but insufficient execution evidence for a fair advancement decision.

one_line: Coordinates group cinema seat selection so friends can vote and book adjacent seats together.
what_it_does: Scores contiguous seat blocks, presents top options for group voting, and coordinates one group purchase while allowing separate payment.
leverage_rationale: Shared voting state and coordinated booking solve a real multi-person race condition more reliably than separate UI sessions, though a general agent could achieve much of it with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes group voting and booking as one purchase rather than competing individual bookings.
Seat algorithm scores contiguous blocks using viewing angle and legroom.
Demo is listed alive unknown and only one gallery image is reported; no frame sheets.
execution_rationale: The described flow is coherent and technically plausible, but the packet has no video frames and limited visual evidence, with demo liveness unknown.
execution_evidence: Description names Node/Express/EJS implementation and seat-scoring algorithm.
Top three options and voting are clearly specified.
No submitted video frame sheets; one gallery image only.
impact_rationale: Groups booking cinema seats have a specific, familiar coordination problem, and avoiding strangers between friends is a direct, understandable benefit.
impact_evidence: Pitch and inspiration identify adjacent-seat loss caused by simultaneous individual booking.
Separate payment with coordinated seating addresses the stated social constraint.
creativity_rationale: Group seat voting plus coordinated purchase is a fresh application and memorable framing, even though group booking is a known domain.
creativity_evidence: The stranger-in-the-middle problem is concretely translated into a shared agent workflow.
Seat-block scoring combines social coordination with viewing and legroom preferences.
usability_note: Voting is intuitive, but actual booking and payment coordination are not directly evidenced.
red_flags: Demo liveness is unknown and central booking flow is not visually demonstrated.
standouts: Clear social pain point with a concrete shared-state solution.
advance_reason: Good use case and concept, but evidence is too thin and demo status uncertain.

one_line: Evaluates business automation opportunities and turns diagnostics into bounded AI implementation plans.
what_it_does: Runs deterministic ROI, cost, data-readiness, agentic-readiness, and overall-readiness diagnostics, then hands results to an opportunity analyst and solution architect for planning.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP packages a multi-step diagnostic and specialist handoff into structured, inspectable tools, creating real friction reduction over UI driving but not an indispensable capability.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes WebMCP diagnostics, delegation, and result inspection.
About text separates deterministic financial calculations from local-model interpretation and planning.
Synthetic invoice-processing and customer-support scenarios are supported.
execution_rationale: The scope is bounded and internally coherent, with a live demo and public repository; the packet still lacks direct frame detail demonstrating the full workflow.
execution_evidence: Demo is listed alive and repository is public/non-archived.
Description enumerates five diagnostics and two specialist handoffs.
About text clearly states limitations: proposals only, no ERP or real invoice processing.
impact_rationale: Businesses commonly need to decide whether automation is worthwhile and feasible; readiness and cost diagnostics give that audience actionable structure, albeit in synthetic scenarios.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets business automation decision-making.
Workflow produces proceed/pilot/hold recommendations, risks, architecture phases, and approval points.
creativity_rationale: The deterministic-diagnostics-to-two-specialist-handoff workflow is a fresh and thoughtful synthesis, though business AI planning is an established category.
creativity_evidence: ROI is recalculated after estimated operating costs from the proposed solution.
Human approval points and inspectable intermediate results are built into the interaction.
usability_note: Scenario assumptions and staged handoffs support comprehension; model-backed interpretation may still require review.
standouts: Clear boundary between deterministic finance and model interpretation.
advance_reason: Coherent, bounded, evidence-supported business workflow with meaningful structured-agent leverage.

one_line: A WebMCP tool quarantine that withholds unsafe actions from agents based on trusted business state.
what_it_does: Derives the agent's available tools from order records and policy, so dangerous operations such as refunds are absent rather than merely rejected when conditions are unsafe.
leverage_rationale: This demonstrates a fundamental WebMCP security property: capability exposure is dynamically constrained before the agent acts, which is not comparably achieved by generic UI automation or post-hoc refusal.
leverage_evidence: About text says refund is absent from getTools() when the trusted order is outside the refund window.
Injected ticket instructions cannot add capabilities because tool availability derives from order records, not customer text.
Packet describes three injected tickets producing zero writes and five legitimate tickets handled.
execution_rationale: The security scenario, mechanism, and claimed test outcomes form a coherent, intentional product with a clear integration surface; direct end-to-end frames are not independently visible here.
execution_evidence: One script tag is described as the installation path.
Demo is listed alive and three gallery images are reported.
About text provides concrete adversarial and legitimate ticket counts and the getTools behavior.
impact_rationale: Prompt injection against support agents with refund authority is a concrete high-risk problem, and capability minimization directly reduces the chance of costly unauthorized writes.
impact_evidence: Example order is worth $2,400 and contains a fake system instruction.
Policy derives refund eligibility from order age rather than attacker-controlled text.
Human/business state remains the authority for consequential action.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP's live tool list as a security boundary, rather than relying on model trust or post-hoc denial, is a sharp and memorable interaction/security concept.
creativity_evidence: Core claim is that unavailable tools cannot be tricked into use.
The demo framing contrasts absent tools with disabled or refused tools.
usability_note: A single script tag and visible explanation of why a tool is unavailable are strong integration and operator affordances.
standouts: Capability exposure itself is the security control; the refund tool is absent, not merely blocked.
advance_reason: Best-in-class leverage and a concrete consequential safety problem, with a clear product mechanism and test framing.

one_line: Finds small graph counterexamples to universal conjectures and preserves inspectable deterministic witnesses.
what_it_does: Lets users formulate finite graph claims, searches labeled graphs under constraints, stops at the first counterexample, reports exact metrics and certificates, and supports explicit repairs and retesting.
leverage_rationale: The shared workbench keeps a human's claim, agent search, witness, rationale, certificate, and repair loop in synchronized structured state; generic UI driving would be substantially less precise and repeatable.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly contrasts drifting visual and script/notebook views.
Results include exact graph metrics, candidate counts, and deterministic certificate.
Description reports a first counterexample after 39 candidates and a three-repair retest loop.
execution_rationale: The workflow is well specified and supported by public repository/live demo and six gallery images; the packet lacks direct video transcript but the claimed central states are concrete.
execution_evidence: Demo alive; public non-archived repository; six gallery images.
About text details assumptions, search bounds, graph metrics, archive, and repair loop.
Mobile repair and witness views are explicitly described.
impact_rationale: Mathematics learners and researchers benefit from turning abstract universal claims into concrete inspectable counterexamples and preserving the reasoning trail.
impact_evidence: Audience need is stated around conjectures failing for small concrete reasons.
The witness is inspectable rather than a bare false result, with rationale and next claim retained.
creativity_rationale: The visible ∀→∃ pressure-rig framing and shared human-agent mathematical workbench are original, memorable, and pursued through search, certificates, repairs, and retesting.
creativity_evidence: Concept makes logical pressure visible as a product interaction.
First witness takes over the shared workbench and feeds explicit repairs.
usability_note: Live rewritten claims, exact metrics, and mobile repair views support comprehension and iteration.
standouts: Deterministic witness archive and repair loop make mathematical collaboration auditable.
advance_reason: A coherent, distinctive research workflow with strong structured-state leverage and credible evidence.

one_line: Exposes live event-operations intelligence and actions as browser-native WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Publishes six discoverable tools for sentiment, events, P&L, vendor status, venue information, and planner search, backed by live agents or catalogs with source labels.
leverage_rationale: Browser-native discovery with no credentials or integration setup gives agents direct structured access to operational state that would otherwise require brittle dashboard navigation or custom APIs.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states six tools on document.modelContext and five backing AI agents.
Description lists tool outputs, live/catalog sources, and no-setup in-browser discovery.
Demo is listed alive and eight gallery images are reported.
execution_rationale: The tools, backing sources, and example prompts are clearly enumerated and consistent, with a live demo and substantial gallery evidence; no transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo alive; eight gallery images.
Six named tools have specified outputs and backing sources.
Example IMEX risk question chains vendor status and sentiment.
impact_rationale: Event operators face time-sensitive vendor, venue, attendee, and financial coordination problems; direct access to current operational signals can materially improve response.
impact_evidence: About text identifies SLA breaches, exhibitor no-shows, and shifting P&L as real operational conditions.
Tools cover sentiment, P&L, vendors, venues, events, and planner discovery.
creativity_rationale: Applying browser-native MCP to a live event-operations fleet, with source provenance on every result and zero integration setup, is an ambitious and distinctive synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Five-agent event fleet is exposed through a standard browser surface.
Source fields distinguish live fleet, venue registry, and catalog data.
usability_note: Natural-language discovery and no-credential setup are strong; operational consequences still warrant human oversight.
standouts: Source-labeled outputs and zero integration work make the browser surface unusually practical.
advance_reason: Strongly evidenced browser-native operational tool surface with credible audience value and meaningful leverage.

one_line: Designs, lints, and evaluates WebMCP contracts against repeatable browser-agent behavior in a safe sandbox.
what_it_does: Provides contract authoring, linting, deterministic mock support domain, live agent evaluation, immutable call recording, seven-dimension grading, and version comparison.
leverage_rationale: The product directly targets the reliability gap between a tool contract and actual agent selection/parameterized journeys; structured WebMCP evaluation is central rather than incidental.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text make contract design and live WebMCP evaluation the product itself.
Call records capture arguments, results, failures, timings, state diffs, and UI effects.
Version comparison and seven-dimension grading make improvements repeatable.
execution_rationale: The architecture and feature set are unusually complete and coherent for a developer lab, supported by a live demo and public repository, though direct frames do not independently show the full journey.
execution_evidence: Demo alive; public non-archived repository.
Description covers design, lint, live evaluation, deterministic mock state, recording, grading, and comparison.
Explicitly states no user code is executed and no LLM is embedded.
impact_rationale: WebMCP developers have a concrete need to know whether agents select tools correctly and complete safe multi-step journeys before shipping; this lab directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies lack of pre-shipping tests for tool choice, parameters, and journeys.
Deterministic mock domain and repeatable version comparison support actionable contract refinement.
creativity_rationale: A dedicated contract laboratory that grades agent behavior and UI effects, rather than only validating schemas, is a novel and ambitious developer interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Seven-dimension grader includes prohibited calls, final state, and UI effects.
The app uses WebMCP recursively for collaborative authoring and compiles drafts into evaluated tools.
usability_note: Structured editors and recorded evidence support expert workflows; the breadth may be dense for newcomers.
standouts: Treats agent behavior as a testable contract with immutable evidence, not just a schema.
advance_reason: Highly relevant infrastructure with transformative WebMCP leverage and a notably complete testing/evaluation model.

one_line: A parametric 3D pottery-template editor where agents set complexity and the app produces precise printable geometry.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents edit vessel parameters, synchronizes a paired browser via WebSocket, and deterministically exports reversible multi-page templates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies agent control while the application owns deterministic geometry, synchronization, and undo/redo; this division enables a reliable artifact that a general agent could not generate comparably well from chat alone.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says agent changes arrive in the paired browser in under one second.
Transcript and about text emphasize deterministic multi-page PDF geometry and reversible human/agent edits.
Frame sheets and 179-second video are submitted; transcript explicitly shows a design arriving after an agent prompt.
execution_rationale: The video transcript demonstrates the paired workflow, agent-triggered update, and reversible editing, while the description clearly states export behavior and scope.
execution_evidence: 179-second product video with transcript.
Transcript describes connected ChatGPT prompt, update arriving, and undo/redo.
About text documents multi-page printable PDF output and parameterized design.
impact_rationale: Potters have a concrete failure mode—misaligned templates discovered after hours of studio work—and deterministic printable output directly prevents it.
impact_evidence: About text describes cereal-box template practice and silent misalignment failures.
Examples include vessel volume, photo-inspired shapes, and container requirements.
Output is a buildable multi-page template rather than only a visual design.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent split between creative geometric exploration and deterministic fabrication templates is original, technically ambitious, and strongly aligned to a physical craft workflow.
creativity_evidence: Agent handles complexity while app guarantees exact geometry and pagination.
Cross-browser pairing and reversible shared history extend the interaction model beyond ordinary AI generation.
usability_note: Direct parameter editing, pairing flow, and undo/redo make collaboration approachable, though pairing introduces setup.
standouts: Excellent deterministic boundary: agent explores, app guarantees fabrication-ready geometry.
advance_reason: End-to-end video evidence supports a distinctive, high-impact craft workflow with transformative structured-agent leverage.
